raw_response:
I only plant cotton on my 7 mu, so I will put my effort there and not spread my money too thin. I do not start from empty thinking. I look at what worked before. Last year I used about the same kind of plan, and people around me also do not dare cut fertilizer too much on cotton, because if the bolls do not set well, the whole year feels wasted. I have a well, so I will use water when the seedlings need it and again when the plants are growing bolls. My land is not big, 7 mu, so family labor can still manage it. I will use improved seed, because I have seen that type do steadier than old seed on nearby fields. For fertilizer, I will not go light. I will put enough base fertilizer and then topdress later, because cotton eats for a long time. I will spray several times through the season, because if I wait until insects get bad, then I lose more money than the spray costs. I will rotary till the land because it is faster and cheaper for my size, and I can finish on time.
